findings.description: The policy grants ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:* and cloudwatch:* (effectively full administrative control over services and all data) on Resource "*" with no conditions. A compromise of this deploy user permits lateral movement, data exfiltration, and persistence across the whole account.

A static IAM access key with full-service permissions is created for the deploy user. Static keys never rotate automatically and cannot be tied to a short-lived role/session, so a leaked key remains valid indefinitely.

The IAM user has no MFA device and no policy requiring multi-factor authentication, yet it holds broad programmatic permissions. Credentials alone are sufficient for full access, removing a key defense against credential theft.

force_destroy = true means the user can be deleted along with attached policies/keys without protection, allowing an accidental or malicious destroy to remove or recreate identities and potentially leave orphaned or hijacked credentials.

The access key material is exported as a root-module output without the sensitive flag, so the secret is written to plan/apply logs and state and is visible to anyone with access to state or CI output.
